title: NCAA Regionals Weekend
blurb: Every D-I and D-III regional, where the nationals fields are decided, plus this week's high school championships, with live results and streams in one place.
seo: NCAA Cross Country Regionals Live Results & Streams
desc: Live results and streams for every 2026 NCAA Division I cross country regional (Nov. 13) and Division III regional (Nov. 14), plus the New Jersey Meet of Champions, the New York state meet, Nike Cross Regionals Heartland and Midwest, and this week's other high school state finals.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Mountain Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Albuquerque, NM
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. MT · Men 10K 12:00 p.m. MT
meets.why: The toughest region in the country. Men: No. 1 New Mexico, No. 2 Colorado, No. 6 BYU and No. 20 Northern Arizona. Women: No. 1 BYU, No. 6 Northern Arizona, No. 7 New Mexico, No. 9 Colorado and No. 16 Utah. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 7 New Mexico won the women’s race with 45 points as Pamela Kosgei (19:08.3), Mercy Kirarei and Marion Jepngetich went 1-2-3, with No. 6 Northern Arizona second (67) and No. 1 BYU third (81). No. 1 New Mexico also took the men’s title, 35 to 42 over No. 2 Colorado, with No. 6 BYU third (65). Texas Tech’s Titus Kimaru won the men’s race in 28:41.9.

meets.name: NCAA D-I South Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Tallahassee, FL · host Florida State · Apalachee Regional Park
meets.time: Women 6K 8:30 a.m. ET · Men 10K 9:30 a.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 4 Alabama, No. 8 Florida and No. 24 Tennessee. Women: No. 4 Alabama and No. 5 Florida. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 4 Alabama’s women won with 21 points behind a 1-2 from Caren Kiplagat (19:20.6) and Cynthia Jemutai, with No. 5 Florida second (74). Alabama’s men won too, 48 to 54 over No. 8 Florida, with No. 24 Tennessee third (120). Florida’s Kelvin Cheruiyot won the men’s race in 29:01.5, 0.7 seconds ahead of Alabama’s Dennis Kipruto.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Midwest Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Ames, IA · host Iowa State · Iowa State Cross Country Course
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. CT · Men 10K 12:00 p.m. CT
meets.why: Men: No. 3 Oklahoma State, No. 10 Iowa State, No. 22 Minnesota, No. 26 Missouri and No. 30 Tulsa. Women: No. 8 Oklahoma State, No. 20 Missouri, No. 25 Iowa State and No. 28 Minnesota. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 25 Iowa State won the women’s race with 72 points over No. 8 Oklahoma State (91), with Betty Kipkore and Rosemary Longisa second and third behind Oklahoma State’s Billah Jepkirui (19:18.9). No. 3 Oklahoma State won the men’s title 57 to 61 over No. 10 Iowa State behind a 1-2 from Brian Musau (28:47.1) and Denis Kipngetich (28:50.0).

meets.name: NCAA D-I Southeast Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Spartanburg, SC
meets.time: Women 6K 10:00 a.m. ET · Men 10K 11:00 a.m. ET
meets.why: Seven ranked women's teams: No. 2 NC State, No. 9 South Carolina, No. 12 Clemson, No. 14 Virginia Tech, No. 18 North Carolina, No. 19 Duke and No. 22 Virginia. Men: No. 9 Wake Forest, No. 15 Virginia Tech, No. 18 Eastern Kentucky and No. 23 Furman. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 2 NC State won the women’s race with 71 points as Hannah Gapes won in 18:42.2, with No. 9 South Carolina second (100) and No. 12 Clemson third (105). No. 9 Wake Forest won the men’s race with 72, and No. 18 Eastern Kentucky edged No. 15 Virginia Tech 104 to 105 for second. Louisville’s Elsingi Kipruto won the men’s race by 16.5 seconds in 28:20.3.

meets.name: NCAA D-I West Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Sacramento, CA · Arcade Creek Cross Country Course
meets.time: Women 6K 9:00 a.m. PT · Men 10K 10:00 a.m. PT
meets.why: Men: No. 5 Oregon, No. 19 Stanford and No. 27 Arizona. Women: No. 11 Oregon, No. 17 Washington State and No. 26 Washington. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 11 Oregon won the women’s race with 38 points over No. 17 Washington State (109), led by winner Diana Cherotich in 18:55.6. No. 5 Oregon’s men won with 51 points ahead of Washington (110) and No. 19 Stanford (115). Washington State’s Solomon Kipchoge won the men’s race in 28:37.6, 12 seconds ahead of teammate Evans Kurui.

meets.name: NCAA D-I South Central Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: College Station, TX · host Texas A&M
meets.time: Women 6K 9:00 a.m. CT · Men 10K 10:00 a.m. CT
meets.why: Men: No. 7 Arkansas and No. 25 Tulane. Women: No. 23 Arkansas. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 23 Arkansas won the women’s race with 51 points ahead of SMU (109) and Stephen F. Austin (113), as Texas A&M-Corpus Christi’s Elizabeth Khatevi won in 18:58.2. No. 25 Tulane beat No. 7 Arkansas 44 to 48 for the men’s title, though Arkansas freshman Nick Busienei won the race in 28:57.1, leading a 1-2 with teammate Ernest Cheruiyot.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Mid-Atlantic Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Bethlehem, PA · host Lehigh
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 10K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 14 Georgetown and No. 17 Villanova. Women: No. 3 West Virginia, No. 24 Penn State and No. 29 Princeton. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 3 West Virginia took the top four places and won the women’s race with 19 points, led by Joy Naukot (19:19.1), with No. 24 Penn State second (83) and No. 29 Princeton third (105). No. 17 Villanova beat No. 14 Georgetown 39 to 56 for the men’s title behind a 1-2 from Bailey Habler (29:47.7) and CJ Sullivan.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Great Lakes Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: East Lansing, MI · host Michigan State · Forest Akers
meets.time: Women 6K 10:00 a.m. ET · Men 10K 11:00 a.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 12 Wisconsin, No. 16 Notre Dame, No. 21 Michigan State, No. 28 Michigan and No. 29 Butler. Women: No. 13 Notre Dame, No. 15 Toledo and No. 21 Northwestern. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 15 Toledo went 1-2-3 behind Karina James (19:55.2) and won the women’s race with 31 points over No. 13 Notre Dame (60). Toledo’s men also won, 59 to 66 over No. 16 Notre Dame, with Michigan State third (106) and No. 12 Wisconsin fourth (109). Butler’s William Zegarski won the men’s race in 29:55.0.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Northeast Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Farmingdale, NY · host Hofstra · Bethpage State Park
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. · Men 10K 12:00 p.m.
meets.why: Men: No. 11 Harvard and No. 13 Syracuse. Women: No. 27 Providence and No. 30 Boston College. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 13 Syracuse won the men’s title with 49 points over No. 11 Harvard (72), and host Hofstra’s Fredrick Kipkosgei won the race in 30:11.0. No. 30 Boston College edged No. 27 Providence 51 to 58 in the women’s race, with Syracuse third (77) and Syracuse’s Keira Rogan the winner in 19:46.9.

meets.name: NCAA D-III Midwest Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Rock Island, IL · host Augustana · Saukie Golf Course
meets.time: Women 6K 12:00 p.m. CT · Men 8K 1:00 p.m. CT
meets.why: The deepest D-III men's region. Men: No. 1 Wartburg, No. 3 North Central (Ill.), No. 12 Chicago, No. 13 Washington (Mo.) and No. 19 Central (Iowa). Women: No. 6 Chicago, No. 8 Washington (Mo.) and No. 20 Wartburg. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 3 North Central (Ill.) won the men’s title with 59 points over No. 1 Wartburg (82), with No. 12 Chicago third (90) and No. 13 Washington (Mo.) fourth (99), though Wartburg’s Isaiah Hammerand won the race in 23:53.7, 12.6 seconds clear of North Central’s Daniel Kasperan. No. 6 Chicago won the women’s title with 33 points, putting five in the top 12, ahead of No. 8 Washington (Mo.) (62) and No. 20 Wartburg (88). Washington’s Lucinda Laughlin won the women’s race in 21:04.6.

meets.name: NCAA D-III North Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Northfield, MN · host St. Olaf · Tostrud Center
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. CT · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. CT
meets.why: Men: No. 5 UW-La Crosse and No. 7 UW-Stevens Point. Women: No. 4 UW-La Crosse, No. 18 Carleton, No. 26 UW-Stevens Point and No. 27 UW-Eau Claire, on the course that hosts nationals a week later. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 4 UW-La Crosse won the women’s race with 32 points, all five scorers in the top 11, ahead of No. 18 Carleton (106) and No. 26 UW-Stevens Point (114), whose Faith Wehrman won in 21:36.4. No. 5 UW-La Crosse also took the men’s title, 52 to 61 over No. 7 UW-Stevens Point, even as Stevens Point’s Mateo Alvarado Venegas (24:27.5) and Logan Murphy went 1-2, a tenth of a second apart.

meets.name: NCAA D-III Mid-Atlantic Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Lock Haven, PA · host Lock Haven · West Branch XC Course
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 2 Johns Hopkins and No. 10 Carnegie Mellon. Women: No. 5 Johns Hopkins and No. 10 Carnegie Mellon. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 5 Johns Hopkins won the women’s race with 37 points over No. 10 Carnegie Mellon (67) behind a 1-2 from Carter Brotherton (20:48.6) and Alexia Tubbs. No. 2 Johns Hopkins edged No. 10 Carnegie Mellon 39 to 41 for the men’s title, packing its scorers from fifth to 10th. Lebanon Valley’s Rory Lieberman won the men’s race in 24:56.8, 3.1 seconds ahead of Carnegie Mellon’s Matthew Short.

meets.name: NCAA D-III East Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: South Portland, ME · host Bates · Wainwright Sports Complex
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 9 MIT, No. 17 Tufts, No. 21 Bates, No. 23 Colby and No. 26 WPI. Women: No. 7 Tufts, No. 9 MIT, No. 21 Bates and No. 30 Colby. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 9 MIT won the men’s race with 44 points over No. 23 Colby (65) and No. 17 Tufts (88), though Colby’s Stephen White won the race in 24:00.2, 0.8 seconds ahead of MIT’s Dylan Fiegener. No. 7 Tufts won the women’s title with 42 points ahead of No. 9 MIT (68) and No. 21 Bates (75), and Bates freshman Charlotte Crum won the women’s race in 21:08.2.

meets.name: NCAA D-III Mideast Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Manchester, CT · host Trinity · Wickham Park
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: Five ranked teams in each race. Women: No. 2 Williams, No. 3 Middlebury, No. 17 Vassar, No. 22 Connecticut College and No. 24 Wesleyan. Men: No. 6 RPI, No. 14 Amherst, No. 16 Williams, No. 18 Wesleyan and No. 24 Middlebury. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 2 Williams won the women’s race with 33 points, ahead of No. 3 Middlebury (71) and No. 17 Vassar (142), whose Haley Schoenegge won in 21:36.3. No. 6 RPI took the men’s title with 33 points over No. 16 Williams (63) and No. 14 Amherst (82), led by race winner Colin Goldschmidt in 25:08.2.

meets.name: NCAA D-III Niagara Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Fredonia, NY · host SUNY Fredonia
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: No. 1 NYU women and No. 13 SUNY Geneseo women; No. 4 SUNY Geneseo and No. 8 NYU men. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 4 SUNY Geneseo won the men’s race with 27 points over No. 8 NYU (52) as Emerson Comer (24:33.8) and James Tette went 1-2. No. 13 SUNY Geneseo also beat No. 1 NYU for the women’s title, 39 to 58, with its five scorers between fifth and 12th. RIT’s Kathryn Arbegast won the women’s race in 21:02.8, 15 seconds ahead of NYU’s Ashlyn Pallotta.

meets.name: NCAA D-III Metro Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Bethlehem, PA · host Moravian · Lehigh Goodman Campus Course
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: No. 22 Haverford men. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 22 Haverford won the men’s title with 23 points over TCNJ (57) behind a 1-2 from Owen Bluman (25:02.0) and Simon Lane. Swarthmore won the women’s race with 43 points ahead of TCNJ (83), and Swarthmore’s Charlotte Martin won by one second over DeSales’ Ellie Kozich in 21:49.8.

meets.name: NCAA D-III Great Lakes Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: East Lansing, MI · host Olivet · Forest Akers East
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 20 Hope, No. 28 Case Western Reserve and No. 30 Calvin. Women: No. 15 Hope, No. 16 Calvin, No. 23 John Carroll and No. 28 Ohio Wesleyan. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 15 Hope edged No. 16 Calvin 84 to 85 for the women’s title, with No. 23 John Carroll third (120), as Rose-Hulman’s Jocelyn Onstot won in 21:52.9. No. 20 Hope swept the team titles by winning the men’s race with 82 points over No. 30 Calvin (111) and No. 28 Case Western Reserve (123). John Carroll’s Sam Su won the men’s race in 24:57.0, 10.2 seconds ahead of Case Western’s Jacob Slater.

meets.name: NCAA D-III South Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Earlysville, VA · host Lynchburg · Panorama Farms
meets.time: First race 10:00 a.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 11 Washington and Lee and No. 27 Lynchburg, the host. Women: No. 14 Emory. Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 11 Washington and Lee won the men’s race with 26 points, placing four in the top five, ahead of No. 27 Lynchburg (70); Matt Kelly (24:42.4) beat teammate Sam Daunt by a tenth of a second. No. 14 Emory won the women’s title with 59 points over Catholic (114) and Christopher Newport (123), and Batten’s Ester Zar won the women’s race by 38.8 seconds in 21:09.6.

meets.name: NCAA D-III West Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Spokane Valley, WA · host Whitworth · The Course Spokane Valley
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. PT · Men 8K 12:00 p.m. PT
meets.why: Men: No. 15 Pomona-Pitzer, No. 25 Claremont-Mudd-Scripps and No. 28 George Fox. Women: No. 11 Pomona-Pitzer, No. 12 Claremont-Mudd-Scripps, No. 19 George Fox, No. 25 Colorado College, No. 29 Whitworth (the host) and No. 30 Trinity (Texas). Nationals bids are on the line for the NCAA D-III Championships on Nov. 21 in Northfield, Minn.
meets.recap: No. 15 Pomona-Pitzer won the men’s race with 40 points over No. 25 Claremont-Mudd-Scripps (85) and Colorado College (144), led by race winner Jefferson Wright in 24:08.1. No. 11 Pomona-Pitzer also won the women’s title with 65 points, ahead of No. 30 Trinity (Texas) (98) and No. 12 Claremont-Mudd-Scripps (102). No. 25 Colorado College’s Charlie Flint won the women’s race in 21:08.9.

meets.name: New Jersey NJSIAA Meet of Champions Cross Country
meets.where: Holmdel, NJ · Holmdel Park
meets.why: New Jersey's fastest runners from every group race together at Holmdel. No. 1 Union Catholic's girls, who scored a perfect 15 at last week's Group meet, go for a fifth straight Meet of Champions title, with No. 19 Ridgewood also in the field. Ocean Township's Leah Starkey, the No. 2 girl in the country, ran 16:45 on this course last week. In the boys race, Union Catholic and No. 16 CBA meet again a week after Union Catholic beat CBA for the Non-Public A title, and CBA's Gavin Schmitt won that race in 15:27.
meets.recap: Ocean Township’s Leah Starkey, the No. 2 girl in the country, won by more than a minute in 16:38.21, faster than her 16:45 on the same course a week earlier. No. 1 Union Catholic won a fifth straight Meet of Champions girls title, led by Cayleigh Kaiser (second, 17:42.46) and Paige Sheppard (third). In the boys race, CBA’s Gavin Schmitt won in 15:17.61, 17.5 seconds ahead of West Windsor-Plainsboro North’s Agrim Jha.

meets.name: Maryland MPSSAA State Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Parkton, MD · Hereford High School
meets.why: Maryland's state final at Hereford High School.
meets.recap: In 4A, Urbana edged Crofton 134 to 138 for the boys title and Walt Whitman won the girls title (74), with Walt Whitman’s Jonah Greszler (15:50.5) and Clarksburg’s Madeline Kelly (18:32.3) winning the races. In 3A, Centennial (boys, 109) and Severna Park (girls, 44) won, with individual titles to Sherwood’s Dimitrios Rementelas (15:53.1) and North Hagerstown’s Mackenzie Philp (18:24.4). Host Hereford swept 2A (boys 104, girls 31) as Eli Aitken won in 16:03.5 and C. Milton Wright’s Brielle Deaner won the girls race (19:07.9), while Smithsburg (boys, 54) and Liberty (girls, 36) won 1A behind winners Dylan Herbst (15:59.8) and Ava Snyder (19:45.9).

meets.name: Arizona AIA State Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Phoenix, AZ · Cave Creek Golf Course
meets.why: Arizona's state final at Cave Creek Golf Course.
meets.recap: Highland won the Division I boys title with 57 points over Mountain View Mesa (107), and Red Mountain’s Crew Comish won the race in 15:37.9. Mountain View Mesa won the D-I girls title, 74 to 93 over Highland, with Cassidy Long the winner in 18:38.6. Flagstaff (boys) and Ironwood Ridge (girls) won Division II, ALA-West Foothills (boys) and ALA-Queen Creek (girls) won Division III, and Hopi swept the Division IV team titles.

meets.name: New England High School Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Belfast, ME · Troy Howard Middle School
meets.why: The top teams and runners from all six New England states, a week after their state meets.
meets.recap: Bishop Hendricken won the boys title by 93 points, 53 to Coe-Brown Northwood’s 146, as Colby Flynn won in 15:03.74 and teammate Shepherd Butler placed fourth. Cumberland edged Exeter 128 to 129 for the girls team title, and Hopkinton’s Madeleine Lane won the girls race in 16:42.10, 9.7 seconds ahead of Exeter’s Alexis Paterna.

meets.name: New York NYSPHSAA State Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Queensbury, NY · Queensbury High School
meets.time: First race 9:30 a.m. ET
meets.why: East Aurora's boys, No. 26 in DyeStat's national team rankings, go for a fourth straight Class C title. Shenendehowa's Riley Lynch (No. 15) and Ithaca's Tsadia Bercuvitz (No. 18) are among the top girls in the country.
meets.recap: No. 26 East Aurora won the Class C boys title with 33 points, 39 ahead of Marcus Whitman, whose Desmond Hill won the race in 15:28.9; Horace Greeley’s Ryan Sykes ran the day’s fastest time, 14:57.6, to win Class B, and Corning’s Christopher Lawson won Class A in 15:07.5. Brighton (A, 75), Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake (B, 63) and Beaver River (D, 64) won the other boys team titles. Nottingham’s Delilah Pandori-Howell won girls Class A in 17:26.0 as Northport took the team title (53), with Ithaca’s Tsadia Bercuvitz third and Shenendehowa’s Riley Lynch seventh, and Sayville (B), Cold Spring Harbor (C) and South Lewis (D) won the other girls titles.

meets.name: Delaware DIAA State Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Felton, DE · Killens Pond State Park
meets.why: Delaware's state final at Killens Pond.
meets.recap: St. Andrews’ Henry Bird ran the fastest time of the day, 15:11.90, to win the Division 2 boys race, and Salesianum’s James Dempsey won Division 1 in 15:49.90. Padua’s Paige Ballinger won the Division 1 girls race in 18:10.60, and Tatnall’s Lauryn Leech won Division 2 in 18:14.80.

meets.name: South Carolina SCHSL State Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Aiken, SC · Aiken Steeplechase
meets.why: South Carolina's state finals at the Aiken Steeplechase, with Classes 5A and 3A in one meet and 4A, 2A and 1A in the other.
meets.recap: Mauldin won the 5A girls title by 50 points over Chapin, and Fort Mill’s Lauren Allen won the race in 18:27. Nation Ford won the 4A boys title as May River’s Jackson Wright won in 15:31. Walhalla swept the 3A boys team and individual titles behind Finn Powell (15:55), and Hanahan edged Christ Church by five points for the 3A girls title as Christ Church’s Charlotte Shew won in 18:31. Greer Middle College swept the 2A team titles.

meets.name: Virginia VISAA State Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Earlysville, VA · Panorama Farms
meets.why: The state championship for Virginia's independent schools, Thursday at Panorama Farms.
meets.recap: Division I: Norfolk Academy won the boys title with 99 points over St. Stephen’s and St. Agnes (107) as Bishop Ireton’s Jason Day won in 15:36.4, and The Potomac School beat Collegiate 56-70 for the girls title as Collegiate’s Virginia Harris won in 18:43.6. Division II: North Cross swept both team titles with 39 points each, led by individual champions Finton Chaney (16:04.1) and Kaitlyn Perkins (19:27.7). Division III: Tandem Friends won the boys title (58) behind Hayes Buppert’s 15:41.0, and Trinity Academy Meadow View edged Timberlake Christian 75-79 for the girls title as Walsingham Academy’s Remington Freeman won in 18:58.2.

meets.name: Nike Cross Regionals Heartland
meets.where: Sioux Falls, SD · Yankton Trail Park
meets.time: Girls 2:25 p.m. CT · Boys 2:55 p.m. CT
meets.why: A Nike Cross Nationals qualifier: the top two teams and top five individuals not on those teams advance. No. 6 Ava Claasen and No. 9 Ruby Ihmels lead the girls race with No. 11 Harrisburg (and No. 16 Brianna Reilly) and No. 17 Pella. No. 27 Sioux Falls Washington and No. 20 Preston Johnson lead the boys.
meets.recap: Ruby Ihmels won the girls race in a course-record 16:23.6, almost 20 seconds ahead of Ava Claasen (16:43.0), and Harrisburg (132) earned a team spot at Nike Cross Nationals. Keegan Decker won the boys race by 0.3 seconds over Jack Crossland in 14:42.5, and Sioux Falls Lincoln/Washington (165) earned an NXN team spot.

meets.name: Nike Cross Regionals Midwest
meets.where: Terre Haute, IN · LaVern Gibson Championship Course
meets.time: Girls 12:30 p.m. ET · Boys 1:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: A Nike Cross Nationals qualifier on the NCAA championship course, with Indiana's Daphne Weller (No. 20 girls) in the field.
meets.recap: Natasza Dudek won the girls race in 16:39.4 and led Purple Track Club to the team title, 141 to Barrington’s 152, with both teams advancing to Nike Cross Nationals. Jack McGovern of Rockhurst won the boys race in 14:32.4.
